scope: Exploratory sensitivity of the previously chosen and now frozen six-input logistic specification. No feature or model selection is performed inside this run.
host_sampling: Sort character host IDs; set.seed(seed + split); sample round(0.3 * host_count) hosts without replacement, matching the published script.
screening_quota: ceil(test_listing_count / 4), identical for both scores within each split
tie_rule: All scores above boundary receive weight 1; tied boundary scores share the remaining quota equally. No outcomes enter the weights.
minimum_stay_imputation: Map observed minimum_nights <= 1 to Yes and > 1 to No. Keep missing values missing. Learn the most frequent observed binary category from training listings only, applying it to missing training and test rows.
mode_tie_rule: No wins an exact tie; stop if no training value is observed.
price_preprocessing: Within-training median by area/type/bedroom segment; unseen test segments use the overall training price median and are counted in the audit.
baseline: Training segment rate smoothed toward training listing prevalence with fixed weight 10; unseen test segments use training prevalence.
model: Unpenalised binomial glm: busy ~ area + dwelling + bedrooms + price_vs_similar_10 + one_night + amenities_10
differences: Logistic minus segment baseline; precision difference in percentage points, AUC and Brier differences in original units. Lower Brier is better.
summary: Equal weight per split. Mean paired difference, median, empirical P05/P95, range, and better/tied/worse counts. The percentile range is sensitivity, not a confidence interval.
selection_history: The binary one-night predictor was chosen after observing that the former 7+ night category contained no positive outcomes. This outcome-informed exploratory choice is fixed here, not reselected within training. Previous property-only nested selection does not validate this new specification.
interpretation: Host separation prevents sharing a host across training and test within a split. Prior exploration and overlapping repeated splits prevent interpreting these results as an untouched external or prospective test. Reviews are not profit.
